info.name: FESS POS — Module API (v1)
info.description:
The POS API the fess_pos module calls (docs/03 §4, docs/08, docs/12). Generated by `fess-pos/tools/postman/build.mjs` — edit it there.

**Environments.** Pick "FESS POS — QA" or "FESS POS — production". Production is **read-only** here: every non-GET request is
skipped (instructions §10–11: no test data on production). QA uses dedicated test users; `tools/postman/provision-qa.ts`
creates them and writes a ready QA environment to `~/.fess-pos/postman/`.

**Order.** Run the folders top to bottom (or run the whole collection): QA setup → exchange → pull → job events → a complete
inspection → other types → card verification → other actions → error cases → sign out. Each request stores what the next
one needs in collection variables. Envelope ids, hashes (RFC 8785 JCS + SHA-256) and device sequence numbers are computed
by the scripts, exactly as the module computes them.

exec: // Shared helpers for every script in this collection:  const pos = eval(pm.variables.get('posLib'));
// Generated by fess-pos/tools/postman/build.mjs — edit it there, not in Postman.
// RFC 9562 UUIDv7: time-ordered, as the module generates ids (docs/03 §7). Test ids only, so Math.random is fine.
for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) r += hex(Math.floor(Math.random() * 16), 1);
const h = hex(Date.now(), 12) + '7' + r.slice(1, 4) + hex((parseInt(r.slice(4, 6), 16) & 0x3f) | 0x80, 2) + r.slice(6);
// RFC 8785 (JCS) for the values an envelope carries: keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, ECMAScript number and string
// serialisation (which JSON.stringify already follows). payload_hash = sha256(JCS(payload)) (docs/12 §11).
if (v === null || typeof v !== 'object') return JSON.stringify(v);
return '{' + Object.keys(v).filter((k) => v[k] !== undefined).sort().map((k) => JSON.stringify(k) + ':' + canonical(v[k])).join(',') + '}';
if (!v) throw new Error('Missing ' + name + ': ' + hint);
// Every device write is an envelope (docs/12 §4): UUIDv7 id, JCS payload hash, per-device sequence number.
api_version: '1', id: id || uuidv7(), type, type_version: 1, payload_hash: hash(payload),
device_id: need('deviceId', 'run "Exchange host token" first'), session_id: pm.collectionVariables.get('sessionId') || null,
if (r.stored_hash && sent[i] && r.state !== 'conflict') pm.expect(r.stored_hash, 'server stored exactly what was sent').to.eql(sent[i].payload_hash);
pm.test('error ' + code + ' with an explicit retryable flag', () => {
// RFC 6238 TOTP (SHA-1, 6 digits, 30 s) for the QA test admin's MFA step.
if (i < 0) throw new Error('adminTotpSecret is not base32');
for (let i = 0; i + 8 <= bits.length; i += 8) key += hex(parseInt(bits.slice(i, i + 8), 2), 2);
// Answers for the seeded global site_inspection v1 form: a standard-risk job at a standalone site, premises
// "complex" (2 external + 2 internal photos, no shopfront). The same set as tools/scenarios/lib/inspection.ts.
const ids = (field) => insp.evidence.filter((c) => c.field_key === field).map((c) => c.id);
nature_of_business: { v: 'General dealer: groceries, airtime and household goods' },
business_hours: { v: { weekdays: { open: '08:00', close: '18:00' }, saturday: { open: '08:00', close: '14:00' }, sunday: 'closed', public_holidays: 'closed' } },
refund_policy: { v: 'Exchange within 7 days with a slip' },
data_security: { v: 'Terminal kept behind the counter; slips filed in a locked drawer; cards never leave the customer.' },
merchant_certification: { v: { given: true, text_version_id: ctx.declarations.merchant, at: iso(new Date(end.getTime() - 5 * 60000)), by_name: 'Thandi Mokoena' } },
agent_declaration: { v: { accepted: true, declaration_version_id: ctx.declarations.agent, accepted_at: iso(end) } },
return { uuidv7, canonical, sha256, hash, iso, getJson, setJson, need, envelope, setIngestBody, checkReceipts, checkError, totp, answersFor };
// Which environment? Production is read-only in this collection (instructions §10–11): no test data, no writes.
if (env !== 'qa' && env !== 'production') throw new Error('Choose the "FESS POS — QA" or "FESS POS — production" environment first.');
console.warn('Skipped on production (read-only in this collection): ' + pm.info.requestName);
else throw new Error('Production is read-only in this collection; only GET requests run there.');

item.description: Public, no key needed. `?deep=1` also checks the database.

item.name: 01 QA setup (test admin)
item.description: QA only. Signs in as the QA test admin (password; the TOTP step runs only if the admin has one set up, D-96), makes a fresh job for the test agent (create, log a contact attempt, confirm the appointment, allocate) and mints the host token a host app would hold for that agent, using the stand-in issuer `pos_dev`. Production refuses the stand-in issuer, and this collection skips every non-GET request there. Run it again whenever you want a fresh job.

item.name: 02 Auth and device
item.description: The module signs in once with the host token and then owns its session: 15-minute access tokens and a rotating, device-bound refresh token (docs/07 §2, D-32). `POST /v1/device` keeps the device registration current (T2-31).

item.name: 04 Ingest — job events
item.description: Every device write is an envelope sent to `POST /v1/ingest` (1–50 per request). The server lands it raw before anything else and answers with one receipt per envelope (docs/12 §4–5). Retries are safe: the same envelope id is a duplicate, never a second effect.

exec: const env = pos.envelope('job_event', { job_id: ctx.job.id, action: 'accept' });

request.description: Same id, same payload: the original receipt comes back as `duplicate`; nothing is applied twice.

exec: if (!env) throw new Error('Run "Accept the job" first');

The server verifies every photo's hash; pg_cron runs the verify worker every 15 s.

item.name: 09 Error cases
item.description: Every API error has the same shape: `{error: {code, message, retryable, details?}, request_id}`. `retryable` tells the module whether to back off and retry or park the item (docs/12 §4).
